instances.h: Polypropylene or stainless steel for a PW loop

block.eyebrow: Technical note 01 · [first note publication month, year] · [note 01 author and reviewer]
block.h: Polypropylene or stainless steel for a PW loop
block.intro: Polypropylene (PP) suits an ambient Purified Water loop, sanitized chemically. Water for Injection (WFI), a hot loop or a stainless standard needs stainless steel. USP <645> and <643> limits, sampling and release stay the same.
rows: Water grade
The loop carries Purified Water (PW) for non-sterile products, rinses and washing.
The loop carries Water for Injection (WFI), or feeds a pure steam generator.
Loop temperature
The loop runs at ambient temperature. Natural PP is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats.
The loop is held hot, or runs routine 80 °C at loop pressure. Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is the plastic option; [whether we quote PVDF].
Sanitization
Chemical sanitization, written as a procedure, with residual tested absent at every outlet before use.
Your procedure calls for routine hot water or steam sanitization.
Your corporate standard
It names outcomes: materials compatible with PW and the sanitizing agent, drainable, with no dead legs.
It names 316L stainless steel for product contact, and a deviation is not an option.
Your clients' audits
Your auditors accept a plastic loop backed by its maker's ratings and your sanitization records.
A client's quality agreement names stainless steel for water contact.
A plastic loop failed before
The cause is known and designed out: joints, supports for expansion, or heat beyond the rating.
No cause was found, and your engineers will not accept plastic again.
